key_insight: PathFM moves beyond predicting separate future values and instead models whole future trajectories, capturing how points in time depend on each other. This makes forecasting more useful for tasks where the shape of the future path matters, not just its marginal uncertainty.
problem_solved: Most time-series foundation models forecast marginal quantiles, which do not specify the dependence structure across future time steps. As a result, they can miss trajectory-level properties like cumulative demand, peak timing, and event sequencing.
method: Uses a trajectory-based forecasting framework rather than independent marginal predictions.
Applies flow matching to generate multivariate future paths efficiently.
Learns the joint structure of trajectories so downstream quantities depending on the full path are better represented.
impact: For practitioners, PathFM offers forecasts that are more actionable when decisions depend on the full future trajectory, such as inventory planning, grid management, and risk analysis. It closes an important gap between standard probabilistic forecasting and real-world path-dependent decision-making.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison of marginal forecasts vs. full trajectory forecasts
A flow-matching pipeline diagram showing input history to generated future path
Example plot of multivariate time series with highlighted cumulative/peak metrics
Icon set for demand, energy load, and event timing applications
paper_title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
paper_authors: Jiachen Yao, Xiyuan Zhang, Annan Yu, Boran Han, Abdul Fatir Ansari
